content: Case reports and anecdotal evidence are insufficient to establish a definitive association between a drug and the risk of birth defects or miscarriage. In animal reproduction studies, no adverse developmental outcomes have been observed with the use of maraviroc. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommend that mothers infected with HIV-1 in the United States refrain from breastfeeding their infants to prevent the risk of postnatal transmission of HIV-1. There is no available data on the presence of maraviroc in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. However, when administered to lactating rats, maraviroc was detected in their milk. Due to the potential risks of HIV transmission to HIV-negative infants, the development of viral resistance in HIV-positive infants, and the possibility of serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants similar to those observed in adults, mothers receiving maraviroc therapy should be instructed not to breastfeed. Maraviroc is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not shown evidence of fetal risk. The drug reaches peak plasma concentration approximately 5 to 4 hours after administration, with a peak level of 333 ng/mL when dosed at 300 mg twice daily. It is 76% protein-bound, has a volume of distribution of 194 liters, and is metabolized primarily by the cytochrome P450 system, with CYP3A being the major enzyme involved. The half-life of maraviroc is approximately 14 to 18 hours, and it is excreted primarily in feces (76%) and urine (20%). Maraviroc is available in tablet and oral solution forms and is typically taken twice daily. It can be administered with or without food but must be used in combination with other antiretroviral medications. The recommended dosage of maraviroc varies depending on concomitant medications due to potential drug interactions. This medication may rarely cause serious liver problems. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction may precede the development of liver issues. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience persistent nausea or vomiting, rash, yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, or extreme fatigue, as these may indicate liver damage or a serious allergic reaction. Maraviroc is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by decreasing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the immune system to function more effectively. This reduces the risk of HIV-related complications, such as opportunistic infections and certain cancers, and improves overall quality of life. Maraviroc belongs to a class of drugs known as entry inhibitors. It is important to note that maraviroc is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, patients should continue taking all HIV medications as prescribed and use effective barrier methods (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms, dental dams) during sexual activity. Personal items that may come into contact with blood or body fluids, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, and razors, should not be shared. Before starting maraviroc, read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist. If using the liquid form of this medication, also review the Instructions for Use. Do not split, crush, or chew the tablet before taking it, as directed by the manufacturer. If using the liquid form, measure the dose carefully with a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. For children, the dosage is also determined by weight. To achieve the best effect, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without consulting your doctor. Common side effects of maraviroc include cough, stomach pain, and fatigue. Lightheadedness or dizziness, particularly when standing, may also occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off previously acquired infections, potentially causing symptoms of these infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time during treatment, even months after starting therapy. A severe allergic reaction to maraviroc is rare. However, if you experience symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, seek medical attention immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking maraviroc, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Maraviroc may cause dizziness, and the use of alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, maraviroc should only be used when clearly needed. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and maraviroc may be part of that treatment. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of maraviroc or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some products that may interact with this drug include orlistat and St. John’s Wort. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load, and T-cell counts, should be performed before starting maraviroc and periodically during treatment. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store maraviroc at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
